163578.latest_action_label: Merger of Maryland University of Integrative Health with Notre Dame of Maryland University (effective February 1, 2024)

landing_actions.action_label: To acknowledge receipt of the complex substantive change request. To include the change in legal status, form of control, and ownership within the institution's scope of accreditation, effective February 1, 2024. To note the complex substantive change request includes the merger of Maryland University of Integrative Health with Notre Dame of Maryland University, effective, February 1, 2024, the anticipated date of the transaction. To require notification of the date of the closing of the transaction within five calendar days of the transaction by email to [email protected] or, if there is a subsequent delay in the anticipated date of the closing of the transaction, to require immediate notification to the Commission of the revised anticipated transaction date. To note that Notre Dame of Maryland University is the surviving institution. To note that the surviving institution is responsible for ensuring the submission of all required reports and information on behalf of the integrated institution. To note the Maryland University of Integrative Health will maintain accreditation for the sole purpose of implementing the teach-out plan and agreements and effectuating the change in ownership process with the United States Department of Education per the United States Department of Education's Updated Guidance and Procedures for Changes in Ownership, dated September 15, 2022 (Electronic Announcement ID: GENERAL-22-70). To note the action for Maryland University of Integrative Health on January 25, 2024. To note that the main campus of Maryland University of Integrative Health at 7750 Montpelier Road, Laurel, MD 20723 will become an additional location included within the scope of accreditation of Notre Dame of Maryland University. To require immediate notification when 7750 Montpelier Road, Laurel, MD 20723 becomes an additional location of Notre Dame of Maryland University by email to [email protected]. To note that the Commission may rescind this action if instruction does not commence within one calendar year from the date of this action. To request a complex substantive change supplemental information report, due July 1, 2024, providing (1) the updated status of the complex substantive change (Substantive Change Policy and Complex Substantive Change Procedures); (2) written evidence of review, including but not limited to, approval of the transaction from all outstanding required licensing, regulatory, or other legal entities as necessary, including the United States Department of Education and the Maryland Higher Education Commission (Standard II); and, (3) written evidence of the institution's updated Eligibility and Certification Approval Report (ECAR) reflecting the inclusion of the additional location. To direct a prompt Commission liaison guidance visit to discuss the Commission's expectations including post-transaction requirements. To direct a complex substantive change site visit to the main campus at 4701 N. Charles Street, Baltimore, MD 21210 and the additional location at 7750 Montpelier Road, Laurel, MD 20723 as soon as practicable but no later than six months after the anticipated date of the transaction, February 1, 2024. To remind the institution of its obligation to inform the Commission about any and all developments relevant to this action. To note the Commission may rescind this action if any development reveals additional information that might have affected the Commission's decision or the complex substantive change is not implemented within one year of this action. To direct the institution to conduct a new comprehensive evaluation in accordance with Commission policy and procedures and federal regulation 34 CFR § 602.22(h). To note that the institution is currently in self-study in anticipation of an evaluation visit in 2025-2026.
landing_actions.action_label_short: Merger of Maryland University of Integrative Health with Notre Dame of Maryland University (effective February 1, 2024)
landing_actions.source_title: MSCHE Statement of Accreditation Status - Notre Dame of Maryland University

landing_actions.action_label: To acknowledge receipt of the complex substantive change request. To include the change in legal status, form of control, and ownership within the institution's scope of accreditation, effective July 1, 2026, the anticipated date of the transaction. To note the complex substantive change request includes the merger of New Jersey City University with Kean University, effective July 1, 2026, the anticipated date of the transaction. To note that the accreditation cease date will be determined after the United States Department of Education (USDE) has approved the merger application. To note that Kean University is the surviving institution. To require notification of the date of the closing of the transaction within five calendar days of the transaction, or immediate notification if there is any delay of the date of the closing of the transaction, by email to [email protected]. To note New Jersey City University will maintain accreditation for the sole purpose of implementing the teach-out plan and agreements and to effectuate the change in ownership process with the United States Department of Education per the United States Department of Education's Updated Guidance and Procedures for Changes in Ownership, dated September 15, 2022 (Electronic Announcement ID: GENERAL-22-70). To note that written documentation of review or approval from the following agency has been received: the New Jersey Office of the Secretary of Higher Education (OSHE) and the New Jersey State Legislature. To request a complex substantive change supplemental information report, due August 17, 2026 providing: (1) the updated status of the implementation of the complex substantive change (Complex Substantive Change Policy and Procedures); (2) an update on the date New Jersey City University's degree granting authority will cease (Requirement of Affiliation 1); and (3) written evidence of review, including but not limited to, approval from all required licensing, regulatory, or other legal entities as necessary, including but not limited to: the United States Department of Education (Standard II). To remind the institution of its obligation to immediately inform the Commission about any and all developments relevant to this action. To note that the Commission reserves the right to rescind this action if any developments reveal additional information that might have affected the Commission's decision and/or the requested substantive change is not implemented within one calendar year from the date of this action. To note the Commission action for Kean University on April 23, 2026.

185262.latest_action_label: Merger of New Jersey City University with Kean University (effective July 1, 2026)

landing_actions.action_label: To acknowledge receipt of the complex substantive change request. To include the change in legal status, form of control, or ownership within the institution's scope of accreditation effective July 1, 2026, the anticipated date of the transaction. To note the complex substantive change request includes the merger of New Jersey City University with Kean University, effective July 1, 2026, the anticipated date of the transaction. To note that Kean University is the surviving institution. To note that the surviving institution is responsible for ensuring the submission of all required reports and information on behalf of the integrated institution. To note that New Jersey City University will maintain accreditation for the sole purpose of implementing the teach-out plan and agreements and effectuating the change in ownership process with the United States Department of Education per the United States Department of Education's Updated Guidance and Procedures for Changes in Ownership, dated September 15, 2022 (Electronic Announcement ID: GENERAL-22-70). To note that the accreditation cease date will be determined after the United States Department of Education (USDE) has approved the merger application. To note that the main campus of New Jersey City University at 2039 Kennedy Boulevard, Jersey City, NJ 07305 will become an additional location included within the scope of accreditation of Kean University. To require immediate notification when New Jersey City University becomes an additional location of Kean University by email to [email protected]. To require notification of the date of the closing of the transaction within five calendar days of the transaction, or immediate notification if there is any delay in the anticipated date of the closing of the transaction by email to [email protected]. To note that written documentation of review or approval from the following agencies has been received: the New Jersey Office of the Secretary of Higher Education (OSHE) and the New Jersey State Legislature. To request a complex substantive change supplemental information report, due September 1, 2026, documenting (1) updated status of the implementation of the complex substantive change (Complex Substantive Change Procedures); (2) written evidence of approvals from all necessary licensing, regulatory, or other legal entities as necessary, including the United States Department of Education (Standard II); (3) evidence of formal conflict-of-interest policies and recusal procedures post-merger transition (Standard II); (4) evidence of individualized credit evaluations and teach-out communication provided to New Jersey City University students (Standard II); (5) sufficient learning experiences and resources to support both the institution's programs of study and the academic progress of all student populations (Standard III); (6) evidence of the integration of New Jersey City University athletic, student life, and other extracurricular activities that are regulated by the same academic, fiscal, and administrative principles and procedures that govern all other programs (Standard IV); (7) evidence of the integration of the New Jersey City University Foundation and its disbursement of scholarship funds (Standard IV); (8) assessment of student learning and achievement that demonstrates that students have accomplished educational goals consistent with their programs of study (Standard V); (9) evidence of migration of New Jersey City University data into the Student Success Data Collaborative (Standard V); (10) evidence that its student learning programs are characterized by coherence and appropriate assessment of student achievement throughout its educational offerings, at both institutional and program levels, with evidence that faculty and appropriate institutional stakeholders have considered and used assessment results to improve teaching and learning (Standard V); (11) the institution's updated Eligibility and Certification Approval Report (ECAR) reflecting the inclusion of the additional location (Standard VI); and (12) evidence of the implementation of a unified governance structure (Standard VII) (Fourteenth Edition and Evidence Expectations by Standard Guidelines). To direct a complex substantive change site visit to the additional location at 2039 Kennedy Boulevard Jersey City, NJ 07305, and to the main campus at 1000 Morris Avenue, Union, NJ 07083, as soon as practicable but no later than six months after July 1, 2026 the anticipated date of the transaction. To remind the institution of its obligation to inform the Commission about any and all developments relevant to this action. To note the Commission may rescind this action if any developments reveal additional information that might have affected the Commission's decision, or the complex substantive change is not implemented within one year of this action. To direct the institution to conduct a new comprehensive evaluation in accordance with Commission policy and procedures and federal regulation 34 CFR 602.22(h). The next evaluation visit is scheduled for 2029-2030. To note the Commission action for New Jersey City University on April 23, 2026.

landing_actions.action_label: To acknowledge receipt of the complex substantive change request. To include the change in legal status, form of control, and ownership within the institution's scope of accreditation, effective June 30, 2024. To note the complex substantive change request includes the merger of Salus University with Drexel University, effective, June 30, 2024, the anticipated date of the transaction. To require notification of the date of the closing of the transaction within five calendar days of the transaction, or immediate notification if there is any delay of the date of the closing of the transaction, by email to [email protected]. To note that Drexel University is the surviving institution. To note that the surviving institution is responsible for ensuring the submission of all required reports and information on behalf of the integrated institution. To note that Salus University will maintain accreditation for the sole purpose of implementing the teach-out plan and agreements and effectuating the change in ownership process with the United States Department of Education per the United States Department of Education's Updated Guidance and Procedures for Changes in Ownership, dated September 15, 2022 (Electronic Announcement ID: GENERAL-22-70). To note the action for Salus University on June 27, 2024. To further note that Salus University will cease accreditation effective June 30, 2025. To include the following additional location within the institution's scope of accreditation effective June 30, 2024: 8630 Old York Road, Elkins Park, PA 19027. To include the following other instructional sites within the institution's scope of accreditation: 7630 Germantown Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19118; 1200 West Godfrey Ave., Philadelphia, PA 19141; 8380 Old York Road, Suite 120, Elkins Park, PA 19027; and 8360 Old York Road, Suite 2100, Elkins Park, PA 19027. To require immediate notification in the institution portal when instruction commences at the additional location. To note that written documentation of review or approval from the following agency has been received: Pennsylvania Attorney General. To request a supplemental information report, due September 30, 2024, providing (1) updated status of the implementation of the complex substantive change (Substantive Change Policy and Complex Substantive Change Procedures); (2) written evidence of review, including but not limited to, approval of the transaction from all required licensing, regulatory, or other legal entities as necessary, including but not limited to: the United States Department of Education and the Pennsylvania Department of Education (Standard II); and (3) written evidence of the institution's updated Eligibility and Certification Approval Report (ECAR) reflecting the inclusion of the additional location. To direct a complex substantive change site visit to the main campus of Drexel University at 3141 Chestnut Street, Philadelphia, PA 19104 and to the additional location at 8630 Old York Road, Elkins Park, PA 19027 as soon as practicable but no later than six months after June 30, 2024, the anticipated date of the transaction. To remind the institution of its obligation to inform the Commission about any and all developments relevant to this action. To note the Commission may rescind this action if any developments reveal additional information that might have affected the Commission's decision or the complex substantive change is not implemented within one year of this action. To direct the institution to conduct a new comprehensive evaluation in accordance with Commission policy and procedures and federal regulation 34 CFR § 602.22(h). To note that the institution will begin self-study in anticipation of an evaluation visit in 2026-2027.

landing_actions.action_label: To acknowledge receipt of the complex substantive change request. To include the change in legal status, form of control, and ownership within the institution's scope of accreditation, effective May 30, 2025. To note the complex substantive change request includes the merger of Keystone College into Keystone College, LLC, with Washington Institute for Education and Research (WIER) as the sole member, effective May 30, 2025, the anticipated date of the transaction. To require notification of the date of the closing of the transaction within five calendar days of the transaction by email to [email protected], or, if there is a subsequent delay in the anticipated date of the closing of the transaction, to require immediate notification to the Commission of the revised anticipated transaction date. To note the institution will maintain its accreditation following the transaction. To note that written evidence of required approvals has been provided by the Pennsylvania Department of Education. To request a complex substantive change supplemental information report, due September 2, 2025, providing (1) the updated status of the complex substantive change; (2) written evidence of review, including but not limited to, approval of the transaction from all outstanding required licensing, regulatory, or other legal entities as necessary, including but not limited to the Pennsylvania Office of Attorney General and the United States Department of Education(Standard II); (3) evidence of a comprehensive financial planning process, multi-year budget, annual independent audit verifying financial viability and internal controls, and documented funding base adequate to support the educational purposes and ensure financial stability that includes a financial development plan and resources from any related entities (Standard VI); (4) planning that integrates goals for institutional effectiveness and improvement, including overall institutional improvement and the results of institutional assessments as related to the complex substantive change transaction and efforts to expand international recruitment (Standard VI); (5) an update on the status of recruiting and hiring a qualified Chief Financial Officer (Standard VI); (6) evidence of the status of the institution's membership in the National Council for State Authorization Reciprocity Agreements and compliance with all membership requirements (Standard VI); (7) evidence of the implementation of a written conflict of interest policy designed to ensure the impartiality of the governing body (Standard VII); and (8) a clearly articulated and transparent governance structure that outlines roles, responsibilities, and accountability for inclusive decision making by each constituency, including the institution's legally constituted governing body and any related entities, including any updates to Keystone College Guide to Governance and Policy (Standard VII) (Fourteenth Edition and Evidence Expectations by Standard Guidelines). To direct a complex substantive change site visit as soon as practicable but no later than six months after May 30, 2025, the anticipated date of the transaction. To note the complex substantive change site visit will occur at the same time as the show cause visit. To direct a prompt Commission liaison guidance visit to discuss the Commission's expectations including post-transaction requirements. To note the Commission reserves the right to rescind this action if any developments reveal additional information that might have affected the Commission's decision and/or the complex substantive change is not implemented within one calendar year from the anticipated date of the transaction. To remind the institution and the related entity of their responsibility for disclosing, documenting, and explaining all significant matters and relationships involving related entities that may impact its compliance including but not limited to governance, independence and autonomy, management and administration, and financial viability and stability (Related Entities Policy and Procedures). To note the Commission's action of February 27, 2025, requiring the institution to show cause why its accreditation should not be withdrawn. The date of the next evaluation will be determined upon reaffirmation of accreditation.

384412.latest_action_label: Required to Show Cause because of insufficient evidence of compliance with Standard II (Ethics and Integrity)

landing_actions.action_label: To acknowledge receipt of the self-study report. To note the on-site evaluation visit by Commission representatives to the main campus at 1401 H Street NW, Washington, DC 20005 on April 7-10, 2024. To note the following branch campus was visited: 7799 Leesburg Pike, Suite 200, Falls Church, VA 22043. To require the institution to show cause, by November 1, 2024, to demonstrate why its accreditation should not be withdrawn because of insufficient evidence that the institution is in compliance with Standard II (Ethics and Integrity), Standard VI (Planning, Resources, and Institutional Improvement), Standard VII (Governance, Leadership, and Administration), and former Requirements of Affiliation 6, 10, 11, 12, and 14. To note that the institution remains accredited while on show cause. To note further that federal regulations limit the period during which an institution may be in non-compliance, which starts on June 27, 2024. To require a show cause report, due November 1, 2024, documenting evidence that the institution has achieved and can sustain ongoing compliance with Commission standards for accreditation, requirements of affiliation, policies and procedures, and applicable federal requirements. The show cause report must include evidence of (1) the institution honoring contracts and commitments, adhering to policies, and representing itself truthfully, in all activities, whether internal or external (Standard II); (2) compliance with all applicable government laws and regulations and Commission policies and procedures, including but not limited to adverse or material actions by all its accrediting and licensing agencies and/or renewals or extensions of approvals by the Higher Education Learning Commission (HELC) and the State Council for Higher Education in Virginia (SCHEV), and other material issues which must be disclosed in a timely and accurate fashion (Standard II, Related Entities Policy and Procedures, and Third-Party Providers Policy and Procedures); (3) institutional and unit goals that are clearly stated, assessed appropriately, linked to mission and goal achievement, reflect conclusions drawn from assessment results, and are used for planning and resource allocation (Standard VI); (4) submission of the fiscal year 2023 audit confirming financial viability and proper internal financial controls, with evidence of corrective measures taken to address any material findings cited in the audit or an accompanying management letter (Standard VI); (5) documentation of the structure, authority, and autonomy of the governing body, including any related entities (Standard VII); and (6) a governing body that makes freely available to the Commission accurate, fair, and complete information on all aspects of the institution and its operations, including but not limited to any third-party provider or related entity, and specifically those entities referenced in the team's findings, and ensuring the institution describes itself in comparable and consistent terms to all of its accrediting and regulatory agencies (Standard VII, Accreditation Review Cycle and Monitoring Policy and Procedures, Related Entities Policy and Procedures, Third-Party Providers Policy and Procedures, and Public Disclosures Policy and Procedures) (Fourteenth Edition and Evidence Expectations by Standard Guidelines). To require that the institution complete and submit for approval, by November 1, 2024, a comprehensive, implementable teach-out plan and signed teach-out agreements with appropriate teach-out partner institutions (Teach-Out Plans and Agreements Policy and Procedures). In accordance with Commission policy and federal regulations, the teach-out plan must provide for the equitable treatment of students to complete their education or transfer to another institution, if the Commission were to withdraw accreditation. To note the Commission may reject the teach-out plan and require resubmission if all of the required information is not provided. To direct an on-site show cause visit following submission of the report. The purpose of the on-site show cause visit is to verify the information provided in the show cause report and the institution's ongoing and sustainable compliance with Commission standards for accreditation, requirements of affiliation, policies and procedures, and applicable federal regulatory requirements. To direct the on-site show cause visit to include the following branch campus: 7799 Leesburg Pike, Suite 200, Falls Church, VA 22043. To direct a prompt Commission liaison guidance visit to discuss Commission expectations. To note that the institution will be invited to present before the Commission when it meets to consider its show cause report. To note that Recommendation Responses in conjunction with the Annual Institutional Update (AIU) are no longer required. To remind the institution of its obligation to provide to the Commission timely and accurate financial audits. The date of the next evaluation will be determined upon reaffirmation of accreditation. To note that additional reporting on Standard V will be required at a date to be determined dependent on the show cause outcome.

accred-zayed-university-united-arab-emir.institution_unique_name: Zayed University, United Arab Emirates | United Arab Emirates
accred-zayed-university-united-arab-emir.latest_action_label: Required to Show Cause because of insufficient evidence of compliance with Standard II (Ethics and Integrity)

landing_actions.action_label: To acknowledge receipt of the self-study report. To note the institution missed the deadline for submission of the self-study report and evidence. To remind the institution of its obligation to submit accreditation materials within established deadlines and in accordance with Commission policy and procedures. To note the on-site evaluation visit by the Commission's representatives to the main campus at Khalifa City, Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates on June 5-9, 2023. To note the following additional location was visited: P.O. Box 19282 Dubai, United Arab Emirates. To require the institution to show cause, by March 1, 2024, to demonstrate why its accreditation should not be withdrawn because of insufficient evidence that the institution is in compliance with Standard II (Ethics and Integrity); Standard VII (Governance, Leadership, and Administration); and former Requirements of Affiliation 6, 12, 13, and 14. To note that the institution remains accredited while on show cause. To note further that federal regulations limit the period during which an institution may be in non-compliance, which starts on November 16, 2023. To require a show cause report, due March 1, 2024, documenting evidence that the institution has achieved and can sustain ongoing compliance with the Commission's standards for accreditation, requirements of affiliation, policies and procedures, and applicable federal regulatory requirements. The show cause report must include evidence that the institution has achieved and can sustain ongoing compliance with Standard II (Ethics and Integrity); Standard VII (Governance, Leadership, and Administration); and former Requirements of Affiliation 6, 12, 13, and 14, including but not limited to (1) compliance with all applicable federal, state and Commission policies and regulations (Standard II and former Requirement of Affiliation 6); (2) public disclosure of required information for students and the public (Standard II and former Requirement of Affiliation 6); (3) substantive changes affecting institutional mission, goals, programs, operations, sites, and other material issues which must be disclosed in a timely and accurate fashion (Standard II and former Requirement of Affiliation 6); (4) a commitment to academic freedom, intellectual freedom, freedom of expression, and respect for intellectual property rights (Standard II and former Requirement of Affiliation 6); (5) a grievance policy that is documented and disseminated to address complaints or grievances raised by students, faculty or staff (Standard II and former Requirement of Affiliation 6); (6) a clearly articulated and transparent governance structure that allows the institution to realize its stated mission and goals in a way that benefits the institution, its students, and the constituencies it serves and outlines roles, responsibilities, and accountability for inclusive decision making by each constituency, including the institution's legally constituted governing body, administration, faculty, staff, and students, as well as any related entities (Standard VII and former Requirements of Affiliation 12, 13, and 14); (7) a legally constituted governing body that serves the public interest, ensures that the institution clearly states and fulfills its mission and goals, has fiduciary responsibility for the institution, and is ultimately accountable for the academic quality, integrity, planning, and fiscal wellbeing of the institution (Standard VII and former Requirements of Affiliation 12, 13, and 14); (8) a governing board that has suﬃcient independence and expertise to ensure the integrity of the institution and whose members have primary responsibility to the accredited institution and that does not allow political, financial, or other influences to interfere with their governing responsibilities (Standard VII); (9) the Chief Executive Officer does not serve as chairperson of the board (Standard VII); and (10) an organizational structure that is clearly documented and that clearly defines reporting relationships with skills, time, assistance, technology, and information systems expertise required to perform their duties (Standard VII) (Fourteenth Edition and Evidence Expectations by Standard Guidelines). To further request that the show cause report demonstrate further evidence of (1) student learning experiences that are designed, delivered, and assessed by appropriately credentialed professionals, sufficient in number, with a core of faculty and/or other appropriate professionals with sufficient responsibility to the institution to assure the continuity and coherence of the institution's educational programs (Standard III); (2) adequate and appropriate institutional review and approval on any student learning opportunities designed, delivered, or assessed by third-party providers, including general education (Standard III); (3) the development and implementation of organized and systematic assessments that evaluate the extent of student achievement of institutional and degree/program goals and that document the use of assessment results to improve educational effectiveness (Standard V); (4) clearly-defined decision-making processes, with clear assignment of responsibility and accountability (Standard VI); and (5) the development and implementation of organized and systematic assessments that evaluate institutional effectiveness, including the assessment of non-academic units (Standard VI). To require that the institution complete and submit for approval, by March 1, 2024, a comprehensive, implementable teach-out plan and signed teach-out agreements with appropriate teach-out partner institutions (Teach-Out Plans and Agreements Policy and Procedures). In accordance with Commission policy and federal regulations, the teach-out plan must provide for the equitable treatment of students to complete their education or transfer to another institution, if the Commission were to withdraw accreditation. To note the Commission may reject the teach-out plan and require resubmission if all of the required information is not provided. To direct an on-site show cause visit following submission of the report and the teach-out plan and teach-out agreements. The purpose of the on-site show cause visit is to verify the information provided in the show cause report and the institution's ongoing and sustainable compliance with the Commission's standards for accreditation, requirements of affiliation, policies and procedures, and applicable federal regulatory requirements. To direct a prompt Commission liaison guidance visit to discuss the Commission's expectations. To note that the institution will be invited to appear before the Commission when it meets to consider the institution's show cause report. To require the institution to submit a substantive change request for the initiation of a new method of delivery (distance education) that is not currently included within the institution's scope of accreditation, due by January 1, 2024 (Standard II and Substantive Change Policy and Procedures). To note that Recommendation Responses in conjunction with the AIU are no longer required. The date of the next evaluation will be determined upon reaffirmation of accreditation.
